stem: When do the rules of the Partnership Act on profit sharing apply?

options.content: When the partners have no agreement on the matter
options.rationale: Correct: the Act supplies terms where the agreement is silent.

options.content: Always, whatever the partners have agreed
options.rationale: A written agreement overrides the default rules.

options.content: Only when the partnership has more than ten partners
options.rationale: The Act applies whatever the number of partners.

options.content: Only when the partnership is dissolved
options.rationale: The rules apply during the life of the partnership.

explanation: The default rules fill gaps; where the partners agree different terms, the agreement prevails.

stem: Under the Partnership Act, with no agreement, how are profits and losses shared?

options.content: Equally between the partners
options.rationale: Correct: whatever the capital or effort.

options.content: In proportion to the capital invested
options.rationale: The Act does not link the ratio to capital.

options.content: In proportion to the time each partner works
options.rationale: Effort is not recognised by the default rules.

options.content: Wholly to the partner who manages the business
options.rationale: No such rule exists.

explanation: The default is equal sharing of profits and losses.

stem: A partner lends money to the partnership beyond his capital and there is no agreement. What interest is the partner entitled to?

options.content: No interest
options.rationale: Interest on loans is the exception to the rule of no interest.

options.content: 5% a year
options.rationale: Correct: this is the rate in the Act.

options.content: 10% a year
options.rationale: The Act sets 5%, not 10%.

options.content: The same rate as the bank overdraft
options.rationale: The Act does not link the rate to the overdraft.

explanation: Under the Act a partner's loan earns 5% a year.

stem: Which of the following is a partner entitled to when there is no agreement?

options.content: A salary for working full time
options.rationale: The Act gives no salary.

options.content: An equal share of the profits
options.rationale: Correct: this is one of the default rules.

options.content: Interest on capital invested
options.rationale: The Act gives no interest on capital.

options.content: Interest on drawings credited to him
options.rationale: No interest is allowed or charged on drawings.

explanation: Only equal sharing and 5% on loans are given by default.

stem: Which is an advantage of a written partnership agreement?

options.content: It removes the need to keep accounts
options.rationale: Accounts are always needed.

options.content: It ensures every partner earns exactly the same profit each year
options.rationale: The agreement may deliberately reward partners differently.

options.content: Unequal effort and capital can be rewarded by salaries and interest
options.rationale: Correct: the Act's equal sharing would otherwise apply.

options.content: It gives the partners limited liability
options.rationale: Partners in an ordinary partnership have unlimited liability whatever the agreement.

explanation: An agreement can include salaries and interest to reflect each partner's input and can set out how disputes are settled.
hints: Think of what the default rules do not provide.

stem: Two partners have no agreement. Profit before interest on a partner's loan is US\$24,600. The loan is US\$8,000. How much profit does each partner receive?

options.rationale: Loan interest has not been deducted first.
The loan interest has been added to one partner's share.
Interest has been deducted twice.

explanation: Loan interest 5% × 8,000 = 400. Profit for the year 24,200 shared equally gives 12,100.
hints: The loan interest is an expense, so deduct it before sharing.

stem: Takudzwa invested US\$30,000 and Mazvita US\$10,000. There is no agreement. Takudzwa claims profit should be shared 3 : 1. What is the position?

options.content: The claim succeeds because capital is the basis of sharing
options.rationale: The Act does not base sharing on capital.

options.content: The claim succeeds because he has more risk
options.rationale: Risk does not alter the default ratio.

options.content: The claim fails because only a court can set a ratio
options.rationale: The Act itself supplies the ratio.

options.content: The claim fails: profits are shared equally under the Partnership Act
options.rationale: Correct: capital does not affect the ratio without an agreement.

explanation: With no agreement, profits are shared equally, however different the capital.
hints: Is there an agreement on ratio?

stem: Partners agreed to share profits 3 : 2 but said nothing about salaries. One partner claims a salary. Which statement is correct?

options.content: A salary is due because the ratio is unequal
options.rationale: The ratio does not imply a salary.

options.content: The agreement is void because it is incomplete
options.rationale: A partial agreement is valid.

options.content: Profits must be shared equally because the agreement is incomplete
options.rationale: The ratio was agreed, so it applies.

options.content: No salary is due; the agreed ratio applies and the default rule of no salary applies
options.rationale: Correct: the Act fills the gap on salaries only.

explanation: Where the agreement is silent on a matter the default rule applies to that matter alone.
hints: The Act applies only where the agreement is silent.

stem: Under the Partnership Act a partner is entitled to a salary if he works full time.
explanation: False. No partner is entitled to a salary unless it is agreed.

stem: Interest on a partner's loan under the Act is an appropriation of profit.
explanation: False. It is an expense of the business, deducted to find profit for the year.
hints: Is the lender acting as owner or creditor?

stem: Match each matter to the rule in the Partnership Act when there is no agreement.
explanation: Equal sharing; no salary; no interest on capital; 5% on loans.

stem: Complete the statement.

payload.template: Without an agreement, interest on drawings is {{blank:a}} and interest on a partner's loan is {{blank:b}} a year.

explanation: No interest is charged on drawings; loans earn 5%.

stem: State the rate of interest on a partner's loan to the firm under the Partnership Act.
explanation: The default rate is 5% a year.

stem: Three partners have no agreement. Profit before interest on one partner's loan of US\$9,600 is US\$28,455. Calculate the share of profit each partner receives.
explanation: Loan interest 5% × 9,600 = 480. Profit for the year 27,975 ÷ 3 = 9,325.
workedSolution: 1. Loan interest 5% × 9,600 = 480. Profit for the year 27,975 ÷ 3 = 9,325.

stem: A partner lent US\$15,000 to the firm on 1 October 2025. There is no agreement. Calculate the interest for the year ended 31 December 2025.
hints: The loan was outstanding for three months.

stem: Partners A, B and C earned a profit for the year of US\$35,940. The agreement gives A a salary of US\$7,000, 5% interest on capital (A US\$42,500, B US\$25,000, C US\$5,000) and the residual shared 2 : 2 : 1. Calculate how much more A receives than under the default rules of the Partnership Act.
explanation: Under the Act each partner receives 35,940 ÷ 3 = 11,980. Under the agreement: residual = 35,940 - 7,000 - 3,625 = 25,315; A receives 7,000 + 2,125 + 2/5 × 25,315 = 19,251. Difference 7,271.
workedSolution: 1. Under the Act each partner receives 35,940 ÷ 3 = 11,980. Under the agreement: residual = 35,940 - 7,000 - 3,625 = 25,315; A receives 7,000 + 2,125 + 2/5 × 25,315 = 19,251. Difference 7,271.
hints: Find A's total under the agreement and under equal sharing.

stem: State two items that are normally included in a partnership agreement.

points.description: Salaries, interest on capital or interest on drawings (or the capital to be contributed, admission and retirement terms, or the dispute procedure)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The ratio in which profits and losses are shared, and any salaries or interest on capital and drawings.

explanation: One mark for each valid item.

stem: Explain two advantages of having a written partnership agreement.

points.description: It prevents disputes because the terms are clear to all partners
It can reward unequal contributions with salaries and interest, instead of equal sharing
It can set out how goodwill is valued and how a partner leaves or joins, avoiding delay and cost

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A written agreement avoids disputes because everyone knows the terms. It can reward a partner who works harder or invests more with a salary or interest. It can also state how goodwill is valued on a change.

explanation: One mark per advantage up to three, each linked to the partnership.
hints: Think about disputes and unequal contributions.

stem: Chipo and Farai have run a printing partnership for three years without an agreement. Chipo works full time; Farai is a sleeping partner who lent the firm US\$20,000. Chipo wants a salary. Evaluate her claim and advise them.

points.description: Under the Partnership Act no partner is entitled to a salary, so her claim has no legal basis without agreement
Equal sharing means Farai receives the same profit despite doing no work, which may be unfair
Farai is entitled to 5% interest on his loan (US\$1,000 a year), which is an expense
Advice: agree and sign an agreement with a fair salary and ratio, since both can change the default

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Without an agreement Chipo has no right to a salary and profits are shared equally, which is unfair to her. Farai is entitled to 5% interest on his loan. They should write an agreement that gives a salary and a ratio reflecting their roles.

explanation: One mark for the legal position, one for fairness, one for the loan interest and one for the advice.
hints: What does the Act say, and can the partners change it?

stem: Four friends, Tendai, Rudo, Sipho and Thandeka, run a catering partnership in Gweru. They never signed an agreement. Sipho lent the business US\$14,000 at the start of the year. Profit for the year ended 31 December 2025 before any interest on the loan was US\$33,280. Tendai works full time and feels she should receive a salary; Rudo, who invested the most capital, thinks profits should be shared in proportion to capital.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the interest due to Sipho on his loan under the Partnership Act.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year to be shared between the partners.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the share of profit received by each partner.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Decide the outcome of each claim under the Act.

left.content: Rudo's claim that profits follow capital
Sipho's claim to interest on his loan

parts.explanation: The Act gives no salary and no link between capital and profit sharing; it gives 5% on loans and equal shares.

explanation: This item tests the default rules of the Partnership Act and their effect on the profit shares.
hints: Deduct the loan interest before sharing.
The default rules apply to each claim.

stem: Mazvita and Takudzwa own a farm-supplies business in Bulawayo. Their agreement provides for a salary of US\$9,500 for Mazvita, interest on capital at 6% a year (Mazvita US\$45,000; Takudzwa US\$16,500) and the residual profit shared 3 : 2. Profit for the year ended 31 December 2025 was US\$47,860. Takudzwa has asked to cancel the agreement and revert to the "legal" arrangement.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (c)

parts.label: (d)

points.description: Without the agreement Takudzwa gains 9,072, which shows why he asks, but Mazvita would lose the reward for her work and capital
The agreement can be changed only by consent of all partners; the Act applies only if there is no agreement
Advice: negotiate a revised agreement reflecting both contributions rather than cancelling it
